svg.text: PROTOMATE / CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION
Motion baseline: evidence and remaining limits
Software correctness, electrical timing and mechanical qualification are separate questions.
Admission and ownership
One exclusive Motor / Axis / Robot family. Reservations include
preparation and cleanup. Protocol, configuration, session, axis
revisions and positions are checked before outputs are armed.
Execution and stopping
M4 maintains immutable schedules with an installed brake.
Explicit stop and lease loss select that branch locally. Abort /
guard inhibition are separate fault paths and can invalidate
referencing.
Memory remains a constraint
M4 fast code and D2 data are close to their linker limits. Each
raw/homing worker reuses its reserved stack after joining.
Command and executor stacks are budgeted separately; no
steady-state motion buffers use the UI heap.
Open blocker: concurrent jog + axis move
The GIGA application can lose its ICC heartbeat during this overlap.
UI reports the reason and shuts down; IO applies local loss
handling. No HardFault was observed. The underlying scheduling /
blocking mechanism is not yet isolated.
Electrical captures pass
Raw: 18 / 18 / 9 pulses. Coordinated: 400 each. Controlled stop:
266 each. HIGH time: 5.00–5.04 µs. Coordinated skew: at most 42
ns. ENABLE remains inactive. These short tests peak near 711
pulses/s.
Remaining verification gaps
Two native ASan/UBSan workflows still time out without a sanitizer
memory report; their cause is unresolved. Lint findings remain. The
6,250-pulse/s ceiling, worst-case latency and powered mechanics
are not qualified by these checks.
Use the review report for exact test outcomes and capture hashes. No diagram claims that a passing short capture proves a full-rate or
mechanically safe operating envelope.
Current source • Normal Release pair: 3be44ebcaf678647 • Electrical tests do not establish mechanical qualification
Sources: Controller / Ownership / StepperMotor; OperatingEnvelope; review report and hardware captures.
